questions.prompt: An ACS receives XML containing an external entity that attempts to read a local server file. What should protect the receiver?

options.text: A hardened XML parser with external entity resolution disabled and controlled input limits
options.explanation: Safe parsing is a prerequisite to processing untrusted protocol input.

options.text: Trusting the XML because it arrived over HTTPS
options.explanation: HTTPS does not make an arbitrary sender's XML safe.

options.text: Base64-decoding twice
options.explanation: Decoding does not prevent XML external entity attacks.

options.text: Checking the user's display name first
options.explanation: Identity fields cannot make unsafe parser behavior acceptable.

questions.prompt: A Response passes schema validation. What has this established?

options.text: Its structure meets the checked schema constraints, not that the issuer is trusted
options.explanation: Structural validity and authenticated origin are different requirements.

options.text: Its signature must be valid
options.explanation: A schema does not perform cryptographic verification.

options.text: Its audience must be the correct SP
options.explanation: A structurally valid audience value can still target another application.

options.text: The local account must be active
options.explanation: Schema checks do not query the local account lifecycle.

questions.prompt: Atlas trusts Okta tenant A for an integration. A response claims tenant B as issuer. What is required?

options.text: Reject or handle it through a separately configured, explicitly expected trust relationship
options.explanation: The expected issuer must be tied to the actual integration and transaction.

options.text: Accept any issuer containing the word Okta
options.explanation: A brand name is not a trust boundary.

options.text: Replace tenant B's issuer with tenant A's string
options.explanation: Editing the message does not authenticate its origin.

options.text: Accept it if another integration already trusts tenant B
options.explanation: A provider trusted for one integration is not automatically the expected issuer for this transaction.

questions.prompt: A response contains a signature, but it does not protect the content the receiver's profile requires. What should the SP do?

options.text: Reject the insufficient protection
options.explanation: Signature presence is not enough; required content and trusted verification must align.

options.text: Accept because any Signature element satisfies every profile
options.explanation: Coverage and verification are essential.

options.text: Accept if the signed part contains a matching display name
options.explanation: Readable matching text does not compensate for missing protection of the content actually required and consumed.

options.text: Copy the signature onto another element
options.explanation: Signatures cannot be transferred to authenticate different content.

questions.prompt: Atlas's entity ID is urn:atlas:prod. An assertion permits only urn:ledger:prod. What follows?

options.text: Atlas must reject the audience mismatch
options.explanation: The assertion is restricted to a different relying party.

options.text: Atlas should accept because both applications use Okta
options.explanation: Shared IdP use does not make audiences interchangeable.

options.text: Atlas should rename itself for this sign-in
options.explanation: Incoming data must not redefine the SP's trusted identity.

options.text: The browser should remove AudienceRestriction
options.explanation: Removing a restriction does not produce a trustworthy assertion.

questions.prompt: An assertion's applicable bearer confirmation names a staging ACS, while the response is being processed at the production ACS. What is the issue?

options.text: The confirmation is not addressed to the actual intended receiving endpoint
options.explanation: Recipient validation ties the bearer confirmation to the appropriate receiver.

options.text: Only the audience needs checking because it identifies the app
options.explanation: Audience and bearer Recipient are distinct targeting requirements; a correct audience does not repair the endpoint mismatch.

options.text: The signing key must necessarily be expired
options.explanation: Target mismatch and key validity are separate checks.

options.text: The assertion must be accepted because staging and production share a company
options.explanation: Environment boundaries remain meaningful within one organization.

questions.prompt: A Response includes Destination pointing to a different endpoint from the receiving ACS. What should the receiver do?

options.text: Enforce the applicable Destination check and reject the mismatch
options.explanation: Destination is an envelope-target check, distinct from audience and bearer Recipient.

options.text: Ignore it if NameID looks correct
options.explanation: Identity text does not repair an envelope target mismatch.

options.text: Treat Destination as the subject's account ID
options.explanation: It identifies a message destination.

options.text: Use it as the post-login resource without checks
options.explanation: Protocol targeting and application navigation are different concerns.

questions.prompt: An assertion has two AudienceRestriction elements. Atlas satisfies one but not the other. Is satisfying one enough?

options.text: No; separate AudienceRestriction conditions must all be satisfied
options.explanation: Alternative audiences inside one restriction differ from multiple restrictions that apply together.

options.text: Yes; all AudienceRestriction elements are always alternatives
options.explanation: That confuses alternatives within a condition with the combination of separate conditions.

options.text: Yes; a signature removes audience restrictions
options.explanation: Signing protects the restrictions rather than cancelling them.

options.text: Yes, if Conditions has not expired
options.explanation: Timing does not remove the separate requirement to satisfy the audience restrictions.

questions.prompt: It is 09:58 at the receiver, and an assertion has NotBefore=10:00. No clock tolerance applies. What should happen?

options.text: Do not accept it yet
options.explanation: The lower bound has not been reached.

options.text: Accept because expiry is later
options.explanation: Both applicable lower and upper time limits matter.

options.text: Rewrite the SP clock based on the assertion
options.explanation: Untrusted input should not set the server's clock.

options.text: Assume NotBefore is only decorative
options.explanation: It expresses a validity condition.

questions.prompt: An assertion narrowly misses a time check. What is an appropriate engineering response?

options.text: Check synchronized clocks, actual timestamps, delivery delays and the configured bounded tolerance
options.explanation: Tolerance is a controlled allowance, not a substitute for understanding the timing evidence.

options.text: Disable all expiry checks
options.explanation: That would remove replay and freshness protections.

options.text: Increase tolerance indefinitely until every assertion works
options.explanation: An unbounded window undermines the intended restriction.

options.text: Treat the IdP's clock as authoritative and ignore the receiver's time
options.explanation: Acceptance needs a trustworthy time basis; blindly adopting incoming timestamps defeats expiry checks.

questions.prompt: An assertion contains two bearer SubjectConfirmation alternatives. One has the right recipient but an expired deadline; the other is timely but has the wrong recipient. What should the SP do?

options.text: Reject because no single applicable confirmation satisfies all required checks
options.explanation: Required fields must hold together within an acceptable confirmation; successful fragments cannot be mixed across alternatives.

options.text: Combine the good recipient from one with the good time from the other
options.explanation: That constructs a confirmation the issuer did not provide.

options.text: Accept because two confirmations are stronger than one
options.explanation: Quantity does not compensate for invalid alternatives.

options.text: Ignore both confirmations and use the display name
options.explanation: Bearer acceptance requires valid subject confirmation, not a name check.

questions.prompt: A signed response names an SP request that belongs to a different browser transaction. What must still be checked?

options.text: The response must match the protected context of the actual sign-in transaction
options.explanation: A real request ID elsewhere in the store is not enough when it belongs to another context.

options.text: Only whether the ID starts with an underscore
options.explanation: Syntax does not establish transaction binding.

options.text: Only whether the assertion's audience names Atlas
options.explanation: Audience is necessary but does not establish the correct browser transaction or pending request context.

options.text: Nothing once the signature is valid
options.explanation: A valid signature does not settle correlation or browser context.

questions.prompt: An attacker submits the same otherwise acceptable assertion twice. What should prevent the second acceptance?

options.text: Appropriate replay detection using the relevant message or assertion identifiers and validity scope
options.explanation: Signature validity persists across copies; replay state is needed to recognize reuse.

options.text: Base64 decoding
options.explanation: The copied encoding remains decodable.

options.text: A new local session ID on each submission
options.explanation: Creating a fresh session for every copied assertion does not detect that the authentication evidence was reused.

options.text: An email-format NameID
options.explanation: Identifier format does not make an assertion single use.

questions.prompt: Atlas runs on three nodes. Each keeps a replay cache visible only to itself. What risk remains?

options.text: The same assertion might be accepted once on each node
options.explanation: Replay protection must cover the active validating service, including concurrency and shared state needs.

options.text: No node can ever verify signatures
options.explanation: Key verification and replay-cache scope are distinct.

options.text: The IdP must issue three different passwords
options.explanation: SAML does not deliver application passwords.

options.text: The load balancer guarantees a copied assertion reaches the original node
options.explanation: Routing behavior should not be assumed to supply the required service-wide replay boundary.

questions.prompt: Two identical responses reach different SP nodes at almost the same instant. Which design matters?

options.text: An atomic consume-or-reject decision across the relevant replay store
options.explanation: A separate check followed later by a write can race, even when both nodes consult the same data.

options.text: A shared cache with an unrestricted check-then-write sequence
options.explanation: Sharing data is not enough if concurrent checks can both succeed before either records consumption.

options.text: Sorting assertions alphabetically
options.explanation: Sorting does not prevent duplicate acceptance.

options.text: Checking a cookie after granting access
options.explanation: A post-acceptance check is too late to guard the acceptance decision.

questions.prompt: Atlas requires a particular authentication context. A valid signed assertion reports a different context. What should happen?

options.text: Apply the configured comparison and assurance requirement before granting the requested access
options.explanation: Trusted reporting does not mean the reported event satisfies every application's requirement.

options.text: Assume every signed context means MFA
options.explanation: The actual context and policy determine assurance.

options.text: Replace the reported context string locally
options.explanation: Editing the result does not change the authentication event.

options.text: Ignore the requirement because the user has an account
options.explanation: Account existence and authentication assurance are separate.

questions.prompt: A receiver encounters an assertion Condition it does not understand and cannot evaluate. What is the safe outcome?

options.text: Do not treat the assertion as valid by simply ignoring that condition
options.explanation: A restriction cannot be assumed satisfied when the receiver cannot evaluate it.

options.text: Ignore any unfamiliar Condition
options.explanation: That can remove an issuer-imposed restriction.

options.text: Interpret it as permission to access everything
options.explanation: Unknown syntax conveys no such permission.

options.text: Ask the browser to delete it
options.explanation: Deleting the condition does not create trusted unrestricted content.

questions.prompt: All SAML acceptance checks pass, but the received identifier has no matching Atlas account and JIT provisioning is disabled. What follows?

options.text: Sign-in cannot complete until the account requirement is resolved
options.explanation: Protocol acceptance does not create an account when the integration does not permit that behavior.

options.text: Create an administrator account automatically
options.explanation: That violates the stated account policy.

options.text: Classify the signature as invalid
options.explanation: The signature can be valid even when local account lookup fails.

options.text: Use a similar account with the same department
options.explanation: A similar account is not a validated unique match for the received identifier.

questions.prompt: Atlas establishes a session for Devi, but Devi lacks the finance-report permission. What should the report request do?

options.text: Deny the report while preserving the distinction from authentication success
options.explanation: Being signed in and being authorized for a particular resource are different outcomes.

options.text: Assume SAML failed entirely
options.explanation: The federation and session creation can have succeeded.

options.text: Grant the report because Okta authenticated her
options.explanation: Authentication alone does not confer every application permission.

options.text: Delete every IdP signing key
options.explanation: Key configuration is unrelated to the missing resource permission.

questions.prompt: A team says, "The assertion is signed, so all remaining checks are unnecessary." Which correction is best?

options.text: A signature is one boundary; targeting, time, correlation, replay, assurance and local eligibility still matter
options.explanation: Acceptance requires the applicable checks to hold together for the actual object consumed.

options.text: Only Base64 decoding matters after a signature
options.explanation: Decoding does not establish those acceptance properties.

options.text: Only a Success status matters
options.explanation: Reported success is not the full receiver decision.

options.text: No signed assertion can ever be replayed
options.explanation: A signed copy can be resubmitted unless replay protection detects it.
